item.title: HBO has revealed a trio of key roles for the second season of its lavish Harry Potter series: Dobby, Ginny Weasley and Tom Riddle, better known as a young Lord Voldemort.
item.description: HBO has revealed a trio of key roles for the second season of its lavish Harry Potter series: Dobby, Ginny Weasley and Tom Riddle, better known as a young Lord Voldemort. 17-year-old British actor, presenter and comedian Lenny Rush will star as Dobby the House-elf, who is introduced in Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets and goes on to play a memorable role later in the series. Rush previously starred in British children's TV series The Dumping Ground, though has also starred in episodes of Doctor Who, as well as Taskmaster. Tom Riddle, meanwhile, will be played by 18-year-old Billy Barratt. While not yet a household name, Barratt is currently filming the Amazon Prime adaptation of hit narrative video game Life is Strange, and also playing an antagonist (Nathan Prescott) in that. If you watched Kraven the Hunter, you'll also have seen him pop up as a young Dmitri Smerdyakov. Lastly, HBO has now confirmed that newcomer Bonnie Hill will portray Ginny Weasley from the series' second season onwards. The character's previous actress dropped out of appearing in future episodes following the show's first season.

item.title: Donald Trump's White House has launched Arcade.Gov, a site with mini-games where you catch and deport immigrants, or use Tetris blocks to build a border wall.
item.description: Donald Trump's White House has launched Arcade.Gov, a site with mini-games where you catch and deport immigrants, or use Tetris blocks to build a border wall. The site's mini-games riff on existing ideas, such as Flappy Bill, an obvious parody of Flappy Bird, which asks players to keep the bill in the air while flying through the capitol. Rio Run, meanwhile, asks you to "patrol the line along the river, pick up every crosser." It's essentially Snake, with you playing a character wearing a business suit, who collects a chain of orange jumpsuited prisoners. At the end of the game, the number of people you have successfully deported is then shown on screen. CAN'T STOP WINNING. 🎮Build the wall. Deport. Fill a Trump Account. LIVE - PLAY NOW 📲 https://t.co/qIR69AxSnm pic.twitter.com/2nr2jG1ZRg

item.title: The Ascent 2 is a game I’ve hoped developer Neon Giant would make ever since I finished the wonderful The Ascent back in 2021 — and after speaking to the studio at gamescom, I’m convinced it’s now in the works.
item.description: The Ascent 2 is a game I’ve hoped developer Neon Giant would make ever since I finished the wonderful The Ascent back in 2021 — and after speaking to the studio at gamescom, I’m convinced it’s now in the works. Neon Giant is currently hard at work on No Law, a first-person Cyberpunk-style game with immersive sim elements set to be published by parent company Krafton. But it has also confirmed plans to turn The Ascent, which has had over 12 million players, into a franchise. “It's something we always wanted to do,” creative director and co-founder Arcade Berg told me. “Creatively, after we were done with the first The Ascent — that was a smashing success for us — creatively, we just wanted to go somewhere else. We weren't ready to do more The Ascent there and then. And team size and also investment wise, we weren't prepared for multiple projects. “But one of the great things that we are now working with Krafton is that we now have backing and support that we can take creative risks. So together with them, we've actually built a franchise plan. We're moving The Ascent from a game to a franchise. And we'll be dropping more news as we figure things out, because it's a longer-term plan. But it's really exciting for us to now know that we have backing and support to do more. And what that is, I can't really go into details of.”

item.title: Translator Emily Wilson is retranslating Homer's The Odyssey from scratch, following her viral critiques calling Christopher Nolan's blockbuster film adaptation "abysmal."
item.description: Emily Wilson strikes again! The University of Pennsylvania professor’s 2017 translation of The Odyssey was an inspiration for Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster movie adaptation, a film that Wilson has slammed as “abysmal” in two recent op-eds that went viral. While Nolan’s film isn’t cited as a reason why, Wilson has revealed that she is translating Homer’s poem all over again. “It’s a complete retranslation. It’s not a revision of the old version,” Wilson told The Associated Press. “I’m about halfway through.” As the AP and the academics they spoke with point out, it’s exceedingly rare for a translator to issue another translation of the same work from scratch. In her first op-ed criticizing Nolan’s The Odyssey, Wilson said she would “be ashamed to have written any part of this script” and that Nolan’s film “lacks psychological, emotional, political, and ethical depth."

item.title: Nintendo has announced a pair of Nintendo Direct broadcasts for next week, including a dedicated Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary showcase.
item.description: Nintendo has announced a pair of Nintendo Direct broadcasts for next week, including a dedicated Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary showcase. The Zelda Direct will air on Tuesday, September 8 at 7am Pacific / 10am Eastern / 3pm UK time, and last 30 minutes. Expect updates on the Zelda franchise, including this year's Ocarina of Time remake, and perhaps a first proper look at next year's live-action Legend of Zelda movie. Nintendo's next general Direct will then air 24 hours later, on Wednesday, September 9 at 7am Pacific / 10am Eastern / 3pm UK time, and last 45 minutes. This will then be followed by a 110-minute Nintendo Treehouse stream, with further gameplay of titles featured in the Direct. I strongly expect Nintendo to show off its Ocarina of Time remake in detail, and give fans more of a sense of how the company has updated its N64 classic. Remember, of course, that Nintendo has confirmed it will launch its Ocarina remake this year — and there's not that much of 2026 left.

item.title: The upcoming Mass Effect-style sci-fi RPG is giving players freedom with relationships and romance options regardless of the gender they choose for their protagonist.
item.description: As you'd expect from a space opera RPG that shares many similarties with Mass Effect, the upcoming Exodus from developer Archetype Entertainment has character relationships that you can build through dialogue choices, interactions, and decisions they make. This includes romance options; while you can choose to play as a male or female version of the lead character Jun Aslan, all character romance options will be available to you. I spoke with Exodus narrative director (and former BioWare narrative lead) Drew Karpyshyn and asked him about how romance options work in this new game. "First of all, the player drives the romances and they are not gender-locked," he told me. Karpyshyn continued explaining the depth of the system and how you can have multiple partners, saying, "There's no situation where a character is going to romance you if you didn't take the initiative. We want to put you in situations where you can potentially try to romance more than one character. Sometimes it'll go well, sometimes it won't depending on the character and depending on the choices you make. Like real life, it's complicated, right? We want it to be complicated." It seems you won't be able to have everyone you want, however, and Exodus is said to pose tough decisions in both story moments and relationship dynamics. "We want to put you in positions where you can't make everybody happy. You're going to have to choose. Who do you side with, knowing that you will gain or lose affinity with one of these companions?" Karpyshyn said, before explaining that the choices you make throughout a playthrough will effect how characters perceive you. And rather than romance being a mechanical type of gameplay system, he mentioned, "We're leaning more toward the romances being a sort of role-playing relationship thing as opposed to being tied directly to gameplay."

item.title: How explicit are the sex scenes in Mass Effect-style game, Exodus? We asked the developers.
item.description: As a big fan of Mass Effect and its various romanceable companions, I wanted to put the record straight on the ins and outs of Exodus’ sex scenes. After all, Exodus looks and feels a lot like Mass Effect. It’s even developed by some of the brains behind BioWare’s much-loved sci-fi RPG franchise. So, it feels reasonable to me to compare and contrast what goes on under the sheets in both games. At gamescom, I interviewed game director Chris King, narrative director Drew Karpyshyn, and general manager Chad Robertson, about all things Exodus, and thought the part of our chat about the sex scenes would be worth closer inspection. I began by asking what to me felt like the most obvious starting point: can you have sex with the octopus? What octopus? Exodus has a number of companions, some of which are non-human. As an 'Awakened' octopus, Salt pilots a specialized combat mech, and can eject ink-like smokescreens that confuse and disorient enemies. She exists in a tank that keeps her alive out on the battlefield. The answer, perhaps unfortunately for some, is no, you can’t have sex with Salt. “Sadly no romance with Salt,” Karpyshyn confirmed. “And that's mostly because Salt just thinks humans are gross. We’ve only got four limbs. She’s like, that’s weird!”

item.title: Hugh Jackman's Wolverine looks set to follow Ryan Reynolds' Deadpool in co-owning an English football team.
item.description: Hugh Jackman's Wolverine looks set to follow Ryan Reynolds' Deadpool in co-owning an English football team. Jackman has long been a fan of Norwich City F.C., a second-tier squad from the east of England nicknamed the Canaries, which has spent the last few decades continually on the bubble of achieving top-level success. Speaking to TalkSport, Jackman mentioned he began supporting Norwich as a child due to it being the birthplace of his mother. And despite growing up in Australia, Jackman has still made various trips to Norwich's home ground over the years. Major cup and league success have proved elusive for Norwich over this time, however, with every successful promotion to the Premier League typically followed by swift relegation the season after. "It's been slim pickings," Jackman admitted of Norwich's success rate over the past four decades. "We did win the Milk Cup in 1984. It's not even called the Milk Cup anymore. But we're on the rise. We're on the up and up.

item.title: PUBG: DED.NET developer Dave Curd has argued that making a video game for the mass market where "nobody's too offended and everybody kind of likes it" has become "box office poison."
item.description: PUBG — the battle royale that popularized the genre — already has a number of spinoffs. But none is as love it or hate it as DED.NET. Like PUBG, DED.NET is a multiplayer first-person shooter that revolves around outlasting your enemies, but there are a number of key differences. Chief among them is roguelite progression that persists across runs, and a heavy-handed 1990s aesthetic dubbed “Grunge House.” But there’s more. Matches — even if you make it to the end — will come in at around the 25-30 minute mark, which makes it a digestible experience relative to PUBG’s more intense, longer-lasting battle royale. And while PUBG is available on console, DED.NET is built from the ground up for consoles. Set in Cascadia in 1996, a world inspired by the Pacific Northwest of the 1990s, and with a reimagining of the PUBG formula beyond battle royale, DED.NET may prove divisive. That, creative director Dave Curd told IGN at gamescom, isn’t just okay — it’s exactly what the developers at Krafton want. In fact, Curd argued that making a game for everyone has become “box office poison.” “Definitely PUBG was the one that brought the genre to prominence and then everyone was like, ‘What's my take? Is it destruction? Is it competitive play? Is it Twitch reactions?’ And you're picturing the games as I'm describing them,” Curd began.

item.title: A flurry of reports point to Marvel secretly mounting a new live-action Disney+ series, potentially featuring characters from the Young Avengers or New Mutants.
item.description: A flurry of reports point to Marvel secretly mounting a new live-action Disney+ series, potentially featuring characters from the Young Avengers or New Mutants. Last month, Murphy's Multiverse spotted that a fresh Marvel production company, Veil Productions, had been set up for a TV project. Now, there's also word on its production codename: "Slumber Party." Marvel typically sets up a production company for each of its major projects, and these can be named something referencing the project itself. (Marvel's recent "Throttle Productions" is believed to be the team behind Ryan Gosling's upcoming Ghost Rider, for example.) So too with its production codenames, though these can also be deliberately obtuse. So, what could Veil refer to? In the Marvel comics, Veil was a young member of the Avengers Academy, and Slumber Party certainly points to a youthful setting. It's also the title of New Mutants #21, which introduced Warlock.

item.title: Last week, France and Saudi Arabia made the surprise announcement that the Paris region of France will be getting a Dragon Ball theme park. This sparked varied reactions across the internet, with many comments in Japanese expressing concern regarding licensing rights and the lack of Japanese representation. This week, Dragon Ball anime producer Toei Animation released an official announcement denying involvement in the project. So what is happening with this proposed Dragon Ball theme park in France?
item.description: Last week, France and Saudi Arabia made the surprise announcement that the Paris region of France will be getting a Dragon Ball theme park. This sparked varied reactions across the internet, with many comments in Japanese expressing concern regarding licensing rights and the lack of Japanese representation. This week, Dragon Ball anime producer Toei Animation released an official announcement denying involvement in the project. So what is happening with this proposed Dragon Ball theme park in France? In case you missed it, Saudi Arabia’s de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman made a two-day state visit to France last month, attending the closing ceremony of the Esports World Cup in Paris alongside French president Emmanuel Macron (source: Arab News). This trip culminated in the surprise announcement of a new theme park project just outside Paris. Posting on X in French on August 25, Macron said: “With Saudi Arabia, we are making an unprecedented announcement.” The French president went on to describe the proposal as three theme parks located in Cergy-Pontoise, northwest of Paris. He cited the 6 billion euro investment and predicted 22,000 jobs created by the project as something that hadn’t been seen “since Disneyland Paris.” It will be a “new global destination — here, in France.” In the post, Macron mentioned his personal liking of Japanese comics (“You know of my interest in manga”), however he did not directly state what themes these three parks would have. However, a later official press release by the Île-de-France region on August 31 referred directly to one of the three being “a Dragon Ball park.”

item.title: Polyphony Digital has revealed Gran Turismo 7’s next major update will mark the return of Autumn Ring, and includes a dozen new cars, the series debut of real-life circuit Sportsland Sugo, and a variety of other features.
item.description: Polyphony Digital has revealed Gran Turismo 7’s next major update will mark the return of Autumn Ring, and includes a dozen new cars, the series debut of real-life circuit Sportsland Sugo, and a variety of other features. The ‘Spec IV’ update will be delivered in two parts before the end of 2026; the first will arrive in October and the second will be available in December. The first chunk of Spec IV will come with Sportland Sugo (a real-life race circuit located in Japan’s Miyagi Prefecture that currently hosts Super GT and Super Formula rounds) plus six new cars, a new ‘Vintage’ section featuring cars not available to purchase in GT as new, a ‘Car Concierge’ function players can use to order used and Legend cars, new driving challenges, a new car viewer, and a Collector Level cap increase. The second half of Spec IV will include Autumn Ring, another six new cars, a new ‘Family’ mode for inexperienced players, a luck-based race with random cars called ‘Shuffle Race’, online drift trials, and a new difficulty level in the Power Pack.

item.title: Dark Souls and Elden Ring director Hidetaka Miyazaki has addressed the rumors that he's got a foot fetish, and he seemed pretty baffled by the whole thing.
item.description: Dark Souls and Elden Ring director Hidetaka Miyazaki has addressed the rumors that he's got a foot fetish, and he seemed pretty baffled by the whole thing. Miyazaki’s games are beloved for their brutal gameplay, grimdark settings, and tortured characters. Of these characters, several of the female bosses, NPCs, and helpers share a common trait: They aren’t wearing any shoes. The Maiden in Black from Demons’ Souls, Sister Friede, Gwunevere, and Priscilla from the Dark Souls games, and even Malenia in Elden Ring all boast bare feet. (Yes, we know Malenia’s legs were destroyed by the Scarlet Rot, but her brother created prosthetics for her that included highly-detailed feet with individual toes. That still counts!) Over the years, this has sparked an inside joke within the Soulslike community, who lightheartedly figured that Miyazaki must be a foot guy. It was never a serious thing — but he brought it up, totally unprompted, during an interview with The Guardian in September 2026.

item.title: Turkish GTA 6 fans want language support so badly that they went out of their way to professionally dub the game's gameplay reveal.
item.description: Turkish GTA 6 fans want language support so badly that they went out of their way to professionally dub its gameplay reveal. The Turkish gaming community has been asking for more and more studios to add Turkish language support for their games. This has led to massive fan campaigns for titles like 007 First Light, which actually resulted in IO Interactive adding Turkish subtitles to the game. Now, the Turkish gaming community is turning their focus to the most anticipated release of the year, if not the most anticipated game in history: Grand Theft Auto 6. Fans have been asking Rockstar Games to add Turkish subtitles or voice overs to GTA 6 ahead of its release in November. They aren't just making social media posts tagging Rockstar, either; they actually professionally dubbed and mixed the entire GTA 6 extended look with a whole cast of actors. The Turkish dub went up just a day after the gameplay was released, which means there was a very fast turn around. It's pretty impressive and shows, there are members of the community actively trying to make this a reality. YouTuber Pintipanda also made a video asking Rockstar to see the potential in localizing GTA 6 for Turkish players. In it, he points out how Turkish-speaking individuals exist in a number of countries outside of Turkey itself, and that GTA 6 is bound to have a wide reach, so it should be as inclusive as possible.

item.title: Dexter: Resurrection Season 2 is bringing back a fan-favorite character that tragically died.
item.description: Spoilers for Dexter: Resurrection Season 1 and seemingly Season 2 follow below. Dexter: Resurrection Season 2 is bringing back a fan-favorite character that tragically died. Deadline has reported that Angel Batista, played by David Zayas, will return in the next season of Dexter: Resurrection. Batista has been in every single season of Dexter in some form since the very beginning, but he met an unfortunate end in Season 1 of Resurrection. After trying to bring Dexter to justice, he ended up being shot and killed by the season's antagonist, Leon Prater. It was a tragic conclusion to the character's arc and one that punished Dexter for trying to have it all. However, Batista will be back once again in Season 2. The actor was seen on set filming a scene with Michael C. Hall in Times Square. Interestingly, he was sporting a more colorful outfit than the last time we saw him, with a Hawaiian shirt, his signature hat, and his gun holster. This seems to suggest that Zayas is returning as one of Dexter's ghosts, preserved in an outfit from when he was a detective in Florida. Various characters have appeared after their deaths to guide or antagonize Dexter over the course of the franchise, but they're not literal ghosts. They're more like manifestations of Dexter's conscience, so Batista may represent some kind of internal guilt for the titular serial killer this time around.

item.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker already has a time-altering mod that largely defeats the purpose of the game.
item.description: The Blood of Dawnwalker already has a mod that largely defeats the purpose of the game. In The Blood of Dawnwalker, a new RPG from ex-CD Projekt Red staff, the player fills the shoes of a man-turned-vampire who has 30 days to save his family. The game has a non-linear story with different approaches, allowing you to progress how you see fit, but there's a catch: Every mission you take on advances the game's 30-day clock. Some quests advance the clock more than others, forcing the player to be thoughtful about quests they accept. Character progression, such as using the skill tree, also advances the clock. Naturally, some fans don't like the pressure this creates. The clock forces them to make tough decisions; it means you have to be choosey about what you do in the game. With that said, it makes sense that its most popular mod completely removes the tension created by this mechanic. The Better Story Timer mod on NexusMods gives you 90 days to do quests, triple the intended amount. This means you don't really have to be precious about the in-game clock or think too hard about your choices. It removes most, if not all, of the friction in The Blood of Dawnwalker. Of course, something like this might make sense a couple of months post-release for those who want to play it differently, but it literally just came out today. The mod has been downloaded almost 10,000 times already, meaning it's pretty popular... but some users have expressed annoyance over players not giving the game a chance in the way it was intended.

item.title: Netflix is cooking up a live-action Dungeons & Dragons TV show based on the tabletop RPG’s gothic-horror campaign, Ravenloft, and its vampire villain, Darklord Strahd von Zarovich.
item.description: Netflix is cooking up a live-action Dungeons & Dragons TV show based on the tabletop RPG’s gothic-horror campaign, Ravenloft, and its vampire villain, Darklord Strahd von Zarovich. The spooky series is penned as an origin story that dives into the events that turned Zarovitch into the vicious vampire count we all know and love today. As told by Variety, Netflix’s Ravenloft show is described as a “prestige fantasy series where adventure collides with gothic horror and tragic romance.” “Ravenloft and its Domains of Dread redefine adventure through character-driven stories of dark magic and supernatural intrigue. At the heart of the series, Ravenloft follows the making of the vampire Darklord Strahd von Zarovich, whose story of power, love, obsession, and undead transformation charts his origins from tragic antihero to one of Dungeons & Dragons’ most notorious villains,” the description reads.

item.title: There's something odd happening on the StarCraft website. While the content still features StarCraft Remastered, which launched back in 2017, the page now seems to be glitching out, with various elements, images, and text blocks flickering on-screen randomly. Could Blizzard be teasing a new StarCraft game?
item.description: There's something odd happening on the StarCraft website. While the content still features StarCraft Remastered, which launched back in 2017, the page now seems to be glitching out, with various elements, images, and text blocks flickering on-screen randomly. Could Blizzard be teasing a new StarCraft game? That would make sense. A report earlier this year said that Blizzard had partnered with Korean gaming giant Nexon to develop a new StarCraft shooter. Blizzard declined to comment on the matter at the time, and the partnership remains unconfirmed, but a report yesterday from South Korean newspaper Chosun (via Wccftech) reaffirms that Nexon is seeking a license to develop a new StarCraft game. Meanwhile, Blizzard may have been working on its own new StarCraft game, as per a 2024 job posting for an "upcoming open-world shooter." Reports from that time suggested the title was in development at Blizzard, led by former Far Cry executive producer Dan Hay, who joined the company in 2022. Another point of evidence is that BlizzCon returns on September 12 after a three-year hiatus, and Blizzard will undoubtedly want to make a splash there with big news beyond its ongoing franchises. There's also a conspicuous hour-long gap on BlizzCon's day-one mainstage programming, while all other panels only have 15 minutes of downtime between them. Sure seems like the place for something that gets announced during the opening ceremonies.

item.title: The directors of Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves, John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein, admitted the fantasy flick flopped due to “not-so-great timing” because of The Super Mario Bros. movie and drama with Wizards of the Coast’s proposed D&D licensing changes.
item.description: The directors of Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves, John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein, admitted the fantasy flick flopped due to “not-so-great timing” because of The Super Mario Bros. movie and drama with Wizards of the Coast’s proposed D&D licensing changes. Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves released in March 2023, right around the time that Wizards of the Coast was facing massive backlash from players after confirming planned adjustments to their Open-Gaming License that would have made sweeping changes to rules that allowed creators to make and sell their own content based on the tabletop RPG’s fifth edition. While they ultimately ended up walking this disastrous decision back, the blowback was enough to negatively impact the movie adaptation, says director John Francis Daley. He claims that this drama, alongside the hugely-successful launch of The Super Mario Bros. Movie around the same time, ultimately overshadowed a film that has since proven to be a hit among fans after the fact. “It was very much a product of not-so-great timing when the first movie came out,” Daley said in an episode of The Discourse Podcast. “It came out four days before the Super Mario movie, which broke records. It came out a month after Wizards of the Coast changed the official gaming license, prompting many D&D fans to boycott the game, and I don’t think the marketing did enough to tell people who weren’t already fans that this movie might be for them. Yeah, so it was a perfect storm of all of those elements, and we’ll see.”

item.title: The Sheriff of Miami-Dade county is speaking out against Miami’s proposal to celebrate the launch of GTA 6 by decking out the city in advertisements for the highly-anticipated game, arguing that it glorifies crime and undermines the efforts of law enforcement.
item.description: The Sheriff of Miami-Dade county is speaking out against Miami’s proposal to celebrate the launch of GTA 6 by decking out the city in advertisements for the highly-anticipated game, arguing that it glorifies crime and undermines the efforts of law enforcement. Grand Theft Auto 6 takes place in Vice City, a fictional version of Miami, Florida. Rockstar took pains to faithfully recreate Miami’s most iconic locales and architecture within the game, with fans already spotting a few real-life locations in the title’s newest trailers. In late August, local news outlets reported that Miami-Dade County officials had spoken with Rockstar Games about potential plans for a Grand Theft Auto 6-themed takeover of Miami, which included ideas like wrapping the Metro line with Vice City branding, creating Vice City manhole covers, and decking out the Miami International Airport with ‘Welcome to Vice City’ signage. While nothing has been formally approved, it seemed like the city was gung-ho for a partnership with the biggest game of the year… but now, the Miami-Dade county sheriff is bringing those ideas to a screeching halt.
